source.locator: Appendix A.1, Corollary 4, and Appendix A.2, Theorem 13 and Corollary 5
source.verbatim_statement: Corollary 4. Numerical edge identifiability is \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hard. Theorem 13. Numerical edge identifiability is in (the promise version of) \(\forall\mathbb R\). Corollary 5. Numerical edge identifiability can be decided in polynomial space.

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2407.12528, Appendix A.1--A.2, HTML version accessed 2026-09-12.

proposed.justification: The theorem gives a deterministic constructive answer to numerical identification exactly below the proposed fan-in boundary.
proposed.gap: Dörfler et al. provide only a polynomial-space numerical test in unrestricted graphs, while Gupta and Bläser and Briefs and Bläser solve generic identification on directed trees; this theorem strictly tightens the numerical upper bound on the fan-in-one class and covers every exceptional covariance.
proposed.consumer: After a latent-to-observed transformation yields maximum indegree one, MIIVsem users can distinguish a failed instrument denominator from genuine nonidentification and receive explicit observationally equivalent coefficient witnesses.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the cited published upper bound used by the theorem's final comparison sentence.

proposed.justification: The exact promise polarity and fiber bijection certify that fan-in two already carries the full universal real-algebraic obstruction.
proposed.gap: Dörfler et al., Corollary 4 and Theorem 13, establish unrestricted promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness, but their Section 4 storage sink has fan-in growing with the source instance; the strict delta is a maximum-directed-indegree-two, fiber-bijective compilation.
proposed.consumer: Algorithm designers for SEM identification obtain a precise reason not to expect a complete polynomial-time extension of the fan-in-one audit to two-parent equations.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the cited unrestricted hardness result used by the theorem's final comparison sentence.
